name: to_local_time
description: Convert one or more source datetimes into your local timezone, with a today/tomorrow/day-N label. ALWAYS call this before describing any source date/time as 'today', 'tomorrow', or any relative day — never do timezone math yourself. Put ALL the datetimes in one call. CRITICAL: pass each time EXACTLY as the source stated it, in the timezone the source named — if a source says '3pm ET' use when '15:00' + tz 'America/New_York'; if it says '20:00 GMT' use tz 'UTC'. Do NOT re-derive a timezone from the venue/city (do not turn 'Seattle' into Pacific or 'Arlington' into Central yourself) and do NOT alter the clock time; copy the source's number and its stated zone verbatim. If the source does not explicitly state a timezone marker, search for another source that does instead of calling this tool. For today/tomorrow answers, include or exclude events solely by the returned relative_day. Pass each event's name as label so every statement in your answer stays bound to that event's converted row.
